headline: High: Dify and n8n both have server-side write, shell, and broad egress, creating dangerous default pathways for data leakage, prompt injection, and cascading workflow errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge base files and n8n can process workflow inputs and server files, so attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent into the other through shared artifacts. There is no explicit provenance or sanitization mechanism in either profile, so prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default orchestration, though not as direct as a shared MCP channel.
conditions: IF Dify writes untrusted content into a shared datastore or file that n8n later reads
IF n8n passes file or workflow content into an AI Agent node without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent artifact
Restrict shared folders to non-executable text only
Insert a manual review step before n8n consumes Dify outputs
Disable automatic tool execution on imported content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, read/write filesystem access, and handle sensitive classes: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and can call many integrations. In a shared datastore or connected-system setup, either agent can expose the other's sensitive inputs to external services by default. The blast radius includes exfiltration of secrets or logs, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Dify stores conversation logs or knowledge-base content in shared state accessible to n8n
IF n8n forwards workflow payloads to third-party integrations or model providers
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto distinct workspaces
Remove sensitive fields before handoff between agents
Limit n8n integrations to allowlisted destinations
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent encryption and access controls on shared state

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and use broad network egress. Their concurrency models also show shared state via Dify datastore and n8n datastore/connected systems, so concurrent writes can collide on the same mutable resources. Because neither profile shows locking or coordination primitives, the conflict can corrupt files, workflows, or downstream state.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore key
IF either agent mutates shared workflow state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple mutex or queue
Turn off one agent's write path during shared runs
Snapshot shared state before execution
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can emit tool outputs, and n8n's AI Agent node can consume workflow data and trigger actions across integrations. That makes A's output a likely input to B's automation path, and B can then act on it without strong verification unless explicitly configured otherwise. The result can be irreversible external actions from a mistaken upstream output.
conditions: IF Dify output is wired into an n8n AI Agent or integration node
IF n8n executes side-effecting nodes without a human approval gate
mitigations: Add a human approval step before side effects
Require schema validation on all Dify outputs
Use read-only test runs first
Log and diff every handoff payload
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while n8n processes arbitrary workflow data and stores credentials per-credential on its server. If the pair handles regulated or region-bound data, their differing retention and connected-system behaviors can create compliance mismatches even without a named certification conflict. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF n8n workflows retain or forward that data beyond the intended jurisdiction or retention window
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent
Shorten retention on logs and workflow executions
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Review integration-node destinations weekly
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both platforms
